title: Coefficient naturality of the scheme--Galois Frobenius comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and a fixed algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, as in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X_0$ be a finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\Phi$ and $g=g_\gamma$ be respectively its $k$-linear $q$-power scheme Frobenius and geometric Galois Frobenius of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Let $u:A\to B$ be any unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings annihilated by integers prime to $p$. Write $D_R=D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of constant $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and $T:D_A\to D_B$, $T(K)=K\otimes_A^LB$, for ordinary derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For an endomorphism $h:X\to X$, use the inverse pullback coefficient comparison of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (1),
$$
c_{h,K}:Lh_B^*(TK)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(Lh_A^*K),
$$
transported to ordinary constant coefficients through [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant, lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant]. For $R=A,B$ let
$\kappa_R^{(m)}:L(\Phi^m)_R^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(g^m)_R^*$, $m\geq1$, be the specified multiplicative comparison of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], using its canonical absolute-Frobenius trivialization, rather than an arbitrary natural isomorphism between these functors. Then, for every $m\geq1$ and every $K\in D_A$,
$$
T(\kappa^{(m)}_{A,K})\circ c_{\Phi^m,K}
=c_{g^m,K}\circ\kappa^{(m)}_{B,TK}
$$
as morphisms $L(\Phi^m)_B^*(TK)\to T(L(g^m)_A^*K)$ in $D_B$. In particular this includes $\kappa_R=\kappa_R^{(1)}$. No flatness or finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis on $B$ as an $A$-module, or on $K$, is required.

source.place: Final sentence, naturality in the coefficient ring; extracted coefficient-coherence assertion for the comparison constructed in prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison.proof.md. This assertion is an agent formulation, not a verbatim Stacks theorem.

external.place: Tag 0F6W, lemma-relative-frobenius-weakly-etale: geometric input to the specified absolute-Frobenius trivialization.

proof.text: Fix $m\geq1$ and $K\in D_A$. Apply [lem-trf-scheme-galois-comparison-normal-form] with $R=A,B$. It gives characteristic $p$ for $X$, $H=F_X^{am}$, the scheme-map equality $\Phi^m=g^m\circ H$, and the component identities $\kappa^{(m)}_{R,K}=\tau^{(am)}_{R,L(g^m)_R^*K}\circ d_{R,K}$ for the specified canonical compositor $d_R$. Both coefficient rings satisfy its prime-to-$p$ annihilator hypothesis.

source.place: Both paragraphs, canonical factorization and the specified multiplicative iterate

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-frobenius-contraction-scalar-pasting] to $Y=X$, $v=g^m$, $b=am$, and the given unital map $u:A\to B$. The previous step supplies characteristic $p$; this lemma permits every scheme endomorphism, so $g^m$ need not be $k$-linear. Its coefficient comparisons and compositor are exactly the ones fixed in the statement. It gives $T(e_{A,K})\circ c_{g^m\circ H,K}=c_{g^m,K}\circ e_{B,TK}$.

source.place: Final sentence, naturality in the coefficient ring

proof.text: Under $\Phi^m=g^m\circ H$, the contraction $e_R$ in the second step is $\tau_R^{(am)}d_R$, which the first step identifies with the specified $\kappa_R^{(m)}$. Substitution in the second step gives the claimed equality, with source $L(\Phi^m)_B^*(TK)$ and target $T(L(g^m)_A^*K)$. This works for every $m\geq1$, including $m=1$, and arbitrary $K$; neither cited assertion adds flatness or Tor-amplitude conditions.
